tools.devsim: DEVSIM 2.11.0 (Apache-2.0), own models via the DEVSIM model API

models.constants: SI 2019 exact q, k_B; eps0 CODATA 2022

electron_phosphorus.locator: Masetti 1983 eq. (1) p. 765, Table I p. 766 phosphorus column

hole_boron.locator: Masetti 1983 eq. (4) p. 767, Table I p. 766 boron column; alpha 0.719 (+-0.013), mu0, mumax, C_r, P_c confirmed in Thurber et al. NBS SP 400-64 (1981) Table 13 p. 40, 300 K; beta 2.00 read from a partly lost scan glyph

models.srh: Shockley and Read 1952 eq. (4.4) p. 837, (5.4) p. 838; n1 = p1 = n_i
models.statistics: Boltzmann, complete ionisation, no bandgap narrowing, no Auger
models.field_dependence: none (Caughey-Thomas factor reported as a post-hoc check)

definitions.V_pn: V(anode, p side) - V(cathode, n side)
definitions.C: q |d N_e,tot / dV|, N_e,tot = integral of n over the device, central difference dV = 2 mV; U = U_mesh + U_dV, U_dV = |C(2 dV) - C(dV)|/3 (max relative over V = 0, -4 V at the finest grid)
definitions.closed_form: depletion approximation W = sqrt(2 eps (V_bi - V)/q (1/N_A + 1/N_D)), C = eps/W; variant with V_bi - V - 2 V_t
definitions.J: total terminal current density (A/cm^2), positive from anode to cathode through the device
definitions.contact_loss_fraction: 1 - q int U_SRH dx / J: share of J carried by minority-carrier recombination at the ideal ohmic contacts (infinite surface recombination) instead of bulk SRH
definitions.contacts: ideal ohmic contacts at both device ends (x = -1 um anode, x = +1 um cathode): charge-neutral equilibrium n, p and psi = V + V_t ln(n_eq/n_i) pinned at the end node; K12: 0.5 um of p+ / n+ between each contact and the i region; K10: 1 um of p / n
definitions.mean_i: trapezoid average (and sheet integral) over the central i region, 0.1 um away from both doping steps (x in [-0.4, 0.4] um); centre = node at x = 0
definitions.E_max_i: max |E| on edges inside the central i region
definitions.caughey_thomas_min_factor: min over the central i region of mu(F)/mu0 = 1/(1 + (mu0 F/v_m)^beta)^(1/beta) with F the quasi-Fermi-level gradient (driving force); post-hoc only, not in the solve
definitions.U: round-2 rule (eoref.util.richardson, p_formal 2) on the three finest grids (h = cell size in nm)
